pois.name: Tokyo National Museum
pois.description: Japan's oldest and largest museum (1872). Houses 110,000+ artifacts including samurai swords, ukiyo-e prints, and the famous Great Buddha statue. The Honkan (Japanese Gallery) is a designated Important Cultural Property.

pois.name: Ueno Station
pois.description: Historic station opened in 1883. Major hub for JR Yamanote, Keihin-Tohoku, and Shinkansen lines. The iconic red-brick facade (designed by Kingo Tatsuno) was restored in 2012.

pois.name: Ueno Park
pois.description: Japan's first public park (1873). 500+ cherry trees bloom in late March–early April. Home to 8 museums, Ueno Zoo (Japan's oldest, 1882), and Shinobazu Pond with its Bentendo Temple.

pois.name: Shinobazu Pond
pois.description: Large freshwater pond in Ueno Park. Rent rowboats in summer, see lotus flowers in July–August. The Bentendo Temple on an island is dedicated to Benzaiten, goddess of water and music.

pois.name: Ameya Yokocho
pois.description: Vibrant market street stretching from Ueno Station to Okachimachi. 400+ shops selling fresh seafood, spices, cosmetics, and street food. The atmosphere is chaotic, colorful, and authentically Tokyo.

pois.name: Ueno Zoo
pois.description: Japan's oldest zoo (1882). Famous for its giant pandas (gift from China in 1972), Sumatran tigers, and the historic 'Garden of Flowers and Birds' monorail (Japan's first, 1952).
